title: rwb-integration booking confirmation (app slice): JOB-08 ownership and event consumer lists, the ACE read boundary, the consumed paths and shapes, the login, the package values and the MSG-P1-001 wording are not settled by one source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 16, 41, 42, 43, 44 and 45; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 15, 16 and 18; TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1, T5.2 and Appendix T-A; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.1, A1.5 and VR-P2-001-1; Ownership Map tables interface_config, outbound_item, job_catalog, decision_record library, and API rows GET /data-products/freshness, POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun (owner P1) and GET /treatments/{treatmentId} (owner S2); legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 16; Template and Rules v1 R3, R5.5, R5.7 and R9
section: 3 Preconditions, 4 Flow, 5 Exception paths, 6 INVEST check, 9 State transitions, 10 Authority, 11 Data, 12.1 to 12.9, 13 Solution plan, 14 Validation and messages, 16 Test cases
description: One combined row for the app slice of this key. (1) Job ownership: Architecture v5 slide 44 names rwb-payment the owner of JOB-08 Booking confirmation and slides 42 and 43 list rwb-payment, not rwb-integration, among the consumers of AceDataReady (EV-26) and TreatmentApproved (EV-10); RWB-P4-E2007-APP and RWB-ITG-E2007-ITG both state that JOB-08 and its activities belong to RWB-P2-E2007-APP, and this story follows that accepted split. (2) ACE read boundary: TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.2 says P2 reads the recovery.v_ace_* views directly and calls nothing in P1 for inbound data, while ADR-010, DP-05 and Architecture v5 slides 41 and 45 make rwb-source-data the only reader of the views and ACE data; the account facts, the batch-completeness answer and the REC-03 write therefore go through the rwb-source-data contract and rwb_integration holds no grant on recovery. (3) Consumed paths and shapes: the legacy story calls the Java interfaces TreatmentQuery.approvedNotBooked, TreatmentCommands.markBooked, TreatmentCommands.recordBookingDifference, AccountQuery.forCase, BatchStatusQuery.forSource, RuleEvaluator.evaluate, TaskApi.raiseTask and the reconciliation writer; no source fixes an HTTP path, a JSON field name or an error for the treatment list, the mark-booked write, the difference write, the case-account read, the reconciliation write or the case task raise, and the treatment single read is the only one with an Ownership Map row. (4) Rerun: the legacy story names POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun; the Ownership Map and API Specification v4 keep that path with x-module P1 as the generic job-catalogue rerun, while this realignment makes JOB-08 a rwb-integration job whose rerun only this service can perform. (5) Login: no source names the per-service login of rwb-integration under DP-02. (6) Package values: package BOOKING_MATCH version BKG-2026.12, its RESTRUCTURE and SETTLEMENT rows and the tolerance 0.00 baht are legacy values of the story master and RWB-E2-042; the row identifiers of the package are the registry's and no source names them in this story, so no rule row ID is written in the criteria. (7) Message text: MSG-P1-001 has two wordings in the sources and FSD P2 Integration v3 gives the current one. (8) Data lake: the legacy REC-03 wording and the legacy section 13 mention reconciliation_result only; DP-17 removes the data lake and nothing in this key builds or sends a lake file.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 44 lists 'JOB-08 | Booking confirmation | Airflow: ACE data ready | rwb-payment | event-triggered workflow'; slides 42 and 43 give the consumer lists of EV-26 and EV-10 without rwb-integration; TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.2 states that P2 reads the views in T1.1 directly; ADR-010 and DP-05 make rwb-source-data the only ACE reader and Architecture v5 slides 41 and 45 repeat it; the legacy RWB-E2-007 section 12 publishes Java interfaces with one HTTP path only; the Ownership Map API row POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun reads owner P1 while job_catalog reads owner P2; the legacy MSG-P1-001 text is 'Today's load has not arrived.' and FSD P2 Integration v3 VR-P2-001-1 gives 'Today's data is not yet complete.'
area: Contract, ownership, ACE read boundary, scheduling, messages
owner_role: Solution architect; contract owners of rwb-treatment, rwb-source-data, rwb-case and rwb-decision; ACE team and DBA
proposed: Keep JOB-08 and its activities with rwb-integration as the sibling stories state and record the rwb-payment owner row of Architecture v5 slide 44 as superseded for this job; read every ACE fact through the rwb-source-data contract and record TSD P2 v3 T5.2 as superseded; fix the six unsettled consumed paths and shapes in RWB-P2-E2007-CON with their owners; serve the rerun on the integration base for the jobs of this service's catalogue; allocate the rwb-integration login in RWB-PLT-DB; keep the BOOKING_MATCH values unchanged and the row identifiers in the registry; take the FSD P2 Integration v3 wording of MSG-P1-001; and confirm that no lake artefact is built for REC-03.

title: rwb-integration booking confirmation (contract slice): the JOB-08 ownership and consumer lists, the ACE read boundary, the rerun placement and the twelve consumed shapes are not settled by one source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 41, 42, 43, 44 and 45; Ownership Map API rows POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun (owner P1), GET /data-products/freshness (owner P1), GET /treatments/{treatmentId} (owner S2) and GET /admin/scheduled-jobs (owner P2); TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1, T5.2 and Appendix T-A (API-P2-009); FSD P2 Integration v3 VR-P2-001-1; legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 3, 4, 7, 11, 12 and 14; Template and Rules v1 R3, R5.5, R5.7 and R9
section: 1 Story, 2 Business rationale, 3 Preconditions, 5 Exception paths, 10 Authority, 11 Data, 12.1 to 12.9, 14 Validation and messages, 18 Traceability
description: One combined row for the contract slice of this key. (1) Job ownership and consumers: Architecture v5 slide 44 names rwb-payment the owner of JOB-08, and the consumer lists of EV-26 and EV-10 do not name rwb-integration, while the accepted split of this legacy key keeps JOB-08 with rwb-integration and adds two consumer rows. (2) ACE read boundary: TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.2 states that P2 reads the recovery.v_ace_* views directly; ADR-010, DP-05 and Architecture v5 slides 41 and 45 supersede it, so the contract declares the account and batch reads as consumed from rwb-source-data and states that rwb_integration holds no grant on recovery. (3) Rerun placement: the legacy path POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun is x-module P1 in API Specification v4 and in the Ownership Map, while the job catalogue read GET /admin/scheduled-jobs is x-module P2; the contract serves the rerun on /api/recovery/integration/v1 for the jobs of this service's catalogue and declares the catalogue read as the base's surface. (4) Consumed shapes: five of the twelve consumed operations and shapes are named only by legacy Java interfaces, and no source fixes their paths, their JSON property names, their required flags or their errors; the Element names this contract fixes are the review baseline. (5) Envelope: the TreatmentBooked payload fields (treatmentId, bookingRef, businessDate) are the legacy story's, and the event type, topic and producer come from the Architecture v5 event catalogue, which no contract document of this key repeats. (6) Messages: MSG-P1-001 has two wordings and FSD P2 Integration v3 gives the current one; the other six texts are the legacy and platform texts unchanged. (7) Identity: no source names the login the contract's clients run as.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 44 lists JOB-08 under rwb-payment; slide 42 lists the consumers of EV-26 as rwb-case, rwb-payment, rwb-deviation and rwb-writeoff and of EV-10 as rwb-comms and rwb-payment; TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.2 keeps the direct view read; the Ownership Map keeps POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun with P1 and GET /admin/scheduled-jobs with P2; the legacy RWB-E2-007 section 12 names the treatment, account, batch, task and reconciliation calls as Java interfaces only; no source in this key publishes a contract document for the match result or the task table.
area: Contract, ownership, ACE read boundary, messages
owner_role: Solution architect; contract owners of rwb-treatment, rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access; platform workflow kit owner
proposed: Baseline the contract with the result shape, the task table, the envelope statement, the rerun operation, the twelve consumed operations and the seven fakes; have the rwb-treatment, rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access contract owners confirm or correct the element names at the review; record the JOB-08 ownership and the TSD P2 v3 T5.2 supersession in the gap register; and confirm the seven message texts in the catalogue.

title: rwb-integration booking confirmation (deployment slice): the login and secret reference, the JOB-08 ownership, the alert thresholds, the runbook ownership and the backfill limit are not fixed by a source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41, 42, 43, 44 and 45; Ownership Map tables job_catalog (P2) and API rows POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun (owner P1) and GET /admin/scheduled-jobs (owner P2); TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1 (job_catalog) and Appendix T-A (API-P2-009); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 15, 16 and 27; FSD P2 Integration v3 VR-P2-001-1; legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 4, 5 and 13; Template and Rules v1 R3, R5.7, R7.2 s12 and R9
section: 3 Preconditions, 10 Authority, 11 Data, 12.5 to 12.7, 13 Solution plan, 14 Validation and messages
description: One combined row for the deployment slice of this key. (1) Identity: no source names the login, the secret reference or the worker identity of rwb-integration under DP-02, and the release must carry one login and one task queue. (2) Job ownership: Architecture v5 slide 44 names rwb-payment the owner of JOB-08 and slides 42 and 43 do not list rwb-integration among the consumers of AceDataReady and TreatmentApproved, while this realignment registers the workflow on the rwb-integration queue; the release registers it there and records the conflict. (3) Schedule absence: JOB-08 is event-started, so the release creates no Schedule and the catch-up and overlap semantics of a Schedule do not apply; no source states the run window that replaces them, so the late-batch alert threshold carries it. (4) Alert thresholds and series definitions: no source fixes the four thresholds, the aggregation window of the four series or the dimensions, and they are values of the environment. (5) Runbook: no source names the four runbook entries, their owner roles or their review cycle. (6) Backfill: no source fixes the backfill limit per run or the reuse window of the Idempotency-Key. (7) Message text: MSG-P1-001 has two wordings and FSD P2 Integration v3 gives the current one; the other four alert texts are the legacy texts unchanged. (8) Build ID: no source fixes the build ID format or the worker versioning policy of this release.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-007 section 13 fixes no deployment value and names no identity; TSD P2 Integration v3 API-P2-009 reads the job catalogue with owner, schedule, run book and alert threshold but names no booking-confirmation row; Architecture v5 slide 44 puts JOB-08 with rwb-payment; the Ownership Map gives job_catalog to P2 and keeps the generic rerun with P1; no source fixes the run window, the four thresholds, the four runbook entries or the backfill limit of this run.
owner_role: DevOps engineer; platform administrator; platform workflow kit owner; business on-call owner for the package alerts
proposed: Fix the identity, the secret reference and the probe checks in RWB-P2-E2007-OPS; register the workflow on rwb-integration and record the JOB-08 owner conflict; take the four thresholds, the series windows and the backfill limit as values of the environment; write the JOB-08 job catalogue row with its run book path; and review the four runbook entries with the on-call rota.
